'''Richard William Beals''' (28 May 1938, [[Erie, Pennsylvania]])<ref>Biographical data from ''American Men and Women of Science'', Thomson Gale 2004</ref> is an American mathematician who works on [[partial differential equations]] and [[functional analysis]]. He is known as the author or co-author of several mathematical textbooks.

Beals studied at [[Yale University]] earning a B.A. in 1960, an M.A. in 1962, and a Ph.D. in 1964 under [[Felix Browder]] with thesis ''Non-Local Boundary Value Problems for Elliptic Partial Differential Operators''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=6610|title=Richard William Beals}}</ref> In the academic year 1965/1966 he was a visiting assistant professor at the [[University of Chicago]], where he became in 1966 an [[assistant professor]] and later a professor. In 1977 he became a professor at Yale University.<ref>{{cite news|title=Yale Mathematician Richard Beals Appointed to Endowed Post|date=6 July 1998|newspaper=YaleNews|url=http://news.yale.edu/1998/07/06/yale-mathematician-richard-beals-appointed-endowed-post}}</ref>

Beals received the [[Quantrell Award]].<ref name="Prize">{{cite web|title=Llewellyn John and Harriet Manchester Quantrell Awards for Excellence in Undergraduate Teaching|url=https://www.uchicago.edu/who-we-are/global-impact/accolades/llewellyn-john-and-harriet-manchester-quantrell-awards-for-excellence-in-undergraduate-teaching|website=UChicago}}</ref>

Beals works on [[inverse problem]]s in [[scattering theory]], [[integrable system]]s, [[pseudodifferential operator]]s, [[complex analysis]], [[Geometric analysis|global analysis]] and [[Transport phenomena|transport theory]]. He has been married since 1962 and has three children.

He should not be confused with the mathematics professor at [[Rutgers University]] named R. Michael Beals (born in 1954), who is Richard Beals's brother.
